changes.finding: C09 duration conversion branches and guard scope
changes.before: Converts finite nonnegative millisecond numbers to fractional Duration values; PTY objects default to 80 by 24 and require dimensions representable as u16.
changes.after: Duration conversion uses Duration::from_millis when as_u64 succeeds; otherwise only finite, nonnegative as_f64 values proceed to Duration::from_secs_f64(ms / 1000.0), without an upper representable-range guard. PTY objects default to 80 by 24 and require dimensions representable as u16.
changes.reason: as_u64 succeeds into Duration::from_millis. The other branch reads as_f64 and checks only finiteness and nonnegativity before calling Duration::from_secs_f64(ms / 1000.0). It has no explicit upper representable-range check. The existing PTY defaults/u16 statement is preserved.

changes.finding: C09 appended floating-point Duration range limit
changes.after: A sufficiently large finite nonnegative value on the floating-point duration branch can exceed Duration's representable range and reach the panicking Duration::from_secs_f64 conversion instead of returning this adapter's Err. schema.rs accepts numeric timeoutMs/graceMs options without that upper bound; this is a source/API boundary, not an observed panic.
preserved_existing_entries: This adapter does not expose maxRssBytes or pipe backpressure at this source revision. hex_bytes consumes pairs and accepts a final single hex digit; schema.rs reuses the same parser rather than requiring even length.
changes.reason: The finite/nonnegative guard does not establish the representable Duration upper bound, and schema options accepts Value::Number without imposing that bound. A sufficiently large finite floating-point millisecond value can therefore reach the standard-library panicking conversion rather than the adapter Err branch. This is the source/API boundary specified in the public correction request, not a runtime panic observation.

api_boundary.property_used: An input exceeding the representable Duration range can panic.

changes.finding: C09 ordinary missing field, missing partial result and scenario-shape validation
changes.before: Only Fail::Product is eligible for pending treatment; malformed or missing expected fields are harness failures.
changes.after: Only Fail::Product is eligible for pending under the suite's other conditions. An absent ordinary field in the returned field map becomes Fail::Harness through string conversion, whereas an expected partial result absent from Error::result() explicitly yields Fail::Product. Malformed expectation shapes are checked during Scenario::load through Names::step and schema::step/schema::expect (including pieces/entries validation), with load errors classified as Harness; the comparator alone is not the complete shape validator.
changes.reason: A missing ordinary field creates a String error that converts to Harness; the partial-result branch explicitly constructs Product when Error::result() is None. Suite classification admits Product as pending only for a listed item, subject to remaining suite checks. Separately, Scenario::load invokes Names::step and schema::step/schema::expect before applicability/execution; schema checks pieces and entries shapes, and suite maps load failures to Harness. Runtime Ctx::step later invokes expect::check. The outcome comparator is not claimed to reject every malformed shape itself.
